subtitle: Where Wooden Votes Ruled Warrior Kings

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a timber assembly hall glowing with lamplight against the dusk, silhouetted chiefs visible within
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma stands at the entrance of a great wooden hall at Vaishali, framed by torchlight as shadowy warriors take their seats inside near the Abhiseka-Pushkarini tank.

dialogue.text: In Vaishali, not one king but many ruled from a hall of wood, where quiet rules and tiny wooden votes decided the fate of a republic.

i18n.hi: वैशाली में एक नहीं, कई राजा लकड़ी की सभा में राज करते थे, जहाँ खामोशी और छोटी लकड़ी की वोटें गणराज्य की किस्मत तय करती थीं।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye view over the Ganga plain, closing in on the fortified mound of ancient Vaishali
panels.action: A sweeping view shows earth ramparts, ponds and groves of Vaishali, with the Abhiseka-Pushkarini tank gleaming beside a cluster of timber buildings on a raised mound.

dialogue.text: Centuries before Ashoka’s pillars and Gupta gold, the land of Vajji held a strange sight: a city where power sat not on one throne, but in an assembly of rajas.

i18n.hi: अशोक के स्तंभों और गुप्तों के सोने से सदियों पहले, वज्जि की धरती पर एक अजीब नगर था, जहाँ सत्ता एक सिंहासन पर नहीं, राजाओं की सभा पर बैठती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level, Saṅghāma walking along the embankment of the sacred tank toward the hall at dawn
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma strides along the edge of the Abhiseka-Pushkarini tank, the water still and misty, as the wooden assembly hall rises beyond, its thatched roof catching the first light.

dialogue.text: The Buddhist texts remember this city as Vaishali, home of the Licchavis, a clan of warrior nobles whose council-hall, the santhagara, bound them together.

i18n.hi: बौद्ध ग्रंथ इसे वैशाली कहते हैं – लिच्छवियों का घर, योद्धा कुलीनों का, जिनकी परिषद-सभा, संथागर, उन्हें एक डोर में बाँधती थी।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of the hall, benches arranged in rows, Saṅghāma inspecting them
panels.action: Inside the wooden hall, Licchavi Saṅghāma runs his hand along sturdy benches and pillars, counting places with a practiced eye as shafts of light fall across empty seats.

dialogue.text: Later stories spoke in awe of seven thousand seven hundred and seven rajas of the Licchavis, a number more poetic than counted, but it hints at their pride in a vast council.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथाएँ हैरानी से बोलती हैं – सात हज़ार सात सौ सात लिच्छवी राजा! गिनती से ज़्यादा कविता, पर उनके विशाल परिषद पर गर्व का इशारा।

panels.shot: close-up on Saṅghāma’s hands untying a cloth bundle of slender wooden slips
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma kneels by a low wooden chest, carefully unwrapping a bundle of slim, polished wooden slips and laying them out in neat rows on a mat.

dialogue.text: There was no paper, no inked ballots. The Vinaya records another world: decisions marked by salaka, narrow wooden tallies, counted by hand under watchful eyes.

i18n.hi: कागज़ नहीं, स्याही नहीं, पर्ची नहीं। विनय एक और दुनिया दिखाता है – जहाँ फैसलों को सलाका, पतली लकड़ी की गिनती से, नंगी आँखों के सामने हाथों से जोड़ा जाता था।

panels.shot: medium shot as Saṅghāma gestures stewards to arrange seat markers along the benches
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma directs attendants placing small wooden pegs or markers along the benches, each slotting into holes that fix where each raja is to sit.

dialogue.text: From these same texts scholars glimpse offices by name: a regulator of seats, a keeper of quorum, a collector of ballots—men who ruled the procedure that ruled the chiefs.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं ग्रंथों में विद्वान पदों की झलक पकड़ते हैं – आसनों का नियामक, गणपूर्ति का रखवाला, वोटों का संग्राहक – वे लोग जो रीति चलाते थे, और रीति से ही सरदार चलते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Saṅghāma at the hall doorway as chiefs approach in small groups
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma stands at the doorway, tall and composed, as groups of armed Licchavi nobles approach, cloaks and hair-knots catching the breeze, their faces wary yet proud.

dialogue.text: This was no democracy of all. The hall belonged to kshatriya lineages. Yet among these few, the way they sat, spoke and voted mattered as much as any spear or chariot.

i18n.hi: यह सबके लिए लोकतंत्र नहीं था। सभा क्षत्रिय वंशों की थी। फिर भी इन चंद लोगों के बीच, वे कैसे बैठते, बोलते और वोट डालते, उतना ही अहम था जितना भाला या रथ।

panels.shot: interior long shot showing nobles taking assigned seats as Saṅghāma oversees
panels.action: Inside, Licchavi nobles file in and take their assigned places along the benches as Licchavi Saṅghāma watches, quietly signaling a steward to shift two men who have sat wrongly.

dialogue.text: The Vinaya’s rules for monks echoed older practice here: seats kept in order, places not snatched, speaking turns observed. A hall unruly in seating foretold a council unruly in mind.

i18n.hi: विनय के भिक्षु-नियम यहाँ की पुरानी रीति दोहराते हैं – आसन क्रम में रखें, जगह न छीनी जाए, बोलने की बारी का मान हो। जो सभा बैठने में बिगड़ी, उसकी बुद्धि भी जल्द बिगड़ती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Saṅghāma counting raised hands or heads while a doorway attendant waits
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma stands at the center, counting rows of faces with his finger while an attendant at the door holds a wooden tally-stick, waiting for his nod.

dialogue.text: The quorum officer’s task was simple and hard: count who has come. If too few sat, no motion could bind the saṅgha. It was a safeguard against decisions taken in thin, sleepy halls.

i18n.hi: गणपूर्ति अधिकारी का काम आसान भी, कठिन भी – गिनना कि कौन आया। लोग कम हों, तो कोई प्रस्ताव संंघ को बाँध नहीं सकता। यह सूनी, सुस्ती भरी सभा के फैसलों से एक पहरा था।

panels.shot: close-up on Saṅghāma’s face as he confers quietly with a senior raja seated at the front
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma leans toward a white-haired chief in the front row, lips close to his ear, as the raja listens with a furrowed brow and nods slowly.

dialogue.text: Texts remember the Buddha advising these same Licchavis to meet in full assemblies, to agree, to follow ancient rules. Even a teacher from outside saw that their strength lay in how they sat together.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ बताते हैं कि बुद्ध ने इन्हीं लिच्छवियों को समझाया – पूरी सभा में बैठो, एक मन से चलो, पुरानी रीति निभाओ। बाहर से आया गुरु भी देख गया कि उनकी ताकत, उनके साथ बैठने में थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Saṅghāma addressing the hall from the center aisle
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma stands in the central aisle, feet planted, hands folded before him, speaking to rows of seated rajas whose eyes are fixed on him in the dim hall.

dialogue.speaker: the_licchavi_santhagara
dialogue.text: Rajas of Licchavi, hear the motion as the elders have framed it.

i18n.hi: लिच्छवी राजाओ, elders ने जैसे प्रस्ताव বাঁधा है, वैसा ही सुनो।

panels.shot: close-up of hands as Saṅghāma demonstrates two different salaka sticks, one slightly notched
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma holds up two slender wooden slips before him, one plain, one with a tiny notch, their grain catching the lamplight as nearby chiefs peer closely.

dialogue.text: The Vinaya lists many ways of casting salakas: open, whispered, secret. A plain slip could mean assent, a marked one dissent, their meaning agreed before any hand reached the basket.

i18n.hi: विनय सलाका डालने की कई तरहें गिनता है – खुली, फुसफुसाहट वाली, गुप्त। सीधी पर्ची सहमति, निशान लगी असहमति, मतलब पहले से ठहर जाता, फिर हाथ टोकरी तक जाते।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Saṅghāma as chiefs whisper and pass slips to an urn
panels.action: From behind Licchavi Saṅghāma, we see chiefs leaning forward to place wooden slips into a large clay bowl, some exchanging brief whispers, others looking away, faces unreadable.

dialogue.text: The ballot-collector moved among them, as monastic rules later describe: calling names, taking each salaka, guarding against double votes, against hasty hands and hidden tricks.

i18n.hi: पर्ची-संग्राहक उनके बीच से गुजरता – जैसा बाद के भिक्षु-नियम बताते हैं – नाम पुकारता, हर सलाका लेता, दोहरी वोट से, जल्दी हाथों से, छिपी चालों से पहरा देता।

panels.shot: close-up of Saṅghāma’s hands sorting the slips into two piles on a mat
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma crouches on the floor, spreading the slips on a mat and sorting them carefully into two piles while a circle of sandaled feet surrounds him.

dialogue.text: Once cast, the slips could not be recalled. The Vinaya insists: the count must be clear, the tally announced, even if some elders frowned at the result that the wood revealed.

i18n.hi: एक बार पर्ची डाल दी, तो लौट नहीं सकती। विनय ज़ोर देकर कहता है – गिनती साफ हो, हिसाब खुलकर सुनाया जाए, चाहे कुछ बुज़ुर्ग लकड़ी से निकले नतीजे पर मुंह क्यों न बना लें।

panels.shot: medium shot of Saṅghāma standing to proclaim the result as the hall leans in
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma rises from his crouch, holding the two sorted bundles of slips, as the seated rajas lean forward, eyes narrowed in anticipation in the flickering light.

dialogue.speaker: the_licchavi_santhagara
dialogue.text: The salakas favor assent. The saṅgha, by majority, accepts the motion.

i18n.hi: सलाका बहुमत को हाँ देती है। संघ बहुसंख्या से प्रस्ताव मान लेता है।

panels.shot: wide shot capturing mixed reactions among the chiefs while Saṅghāma remains composed
panels.action: Around Licchavi Saṅghāma, some rajas smile, some look grim, one stares at the floor, yet the hall holds its order as he stands still at the center, expression calm.

dialogue.text: Victory and displeasure shared the same benches. Yet the procedure stood above both, for if the rules frayed, so did the very idea that the saṅgha could bind its own warriors.

i18n.hi: जीत और नाराज़ी एक ही बेंच पर बैठती थीं। पर रीति दोनों से ऊपर खड़ी रहती, क्योंकि अगर नियम टूटते, तो यही सोच भी टूटती कि संघ अपने ही योद्धाओं को बाँध सकता है।

panels.shot: exterior shot of the hall later that day, Saṅghāma exiting as farmers and traders move in the foreground
panels.action: Licchavi Saṅghāma steps out of the hall into sunlight as farmers drive carts and traders lead pack animals nearby, the life of Vaishali flowing around the quiet building.

dialogue.text: Outside, farmers and merchants did not sit in this hall. Yet its decisions shaped their taxes, their security, even their gods, through wars declared and alliances woven within.

i18n.hi: बाहर किसान और व्यापारी इस सभा में नहीं बैठते थे। पर यहीं के फैसले उनके कर, उनकी सुरक्षा, उनके देवता तक तय करते – युद्धों की घोषणा से, भीतर बुनी गई सन्धियों तक।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of the hall fading as centuries pass, replaced by ruins and earthworks
panels.action: The solid wooden hall dissolves into an empty mound with faint earth embankments, as grass and shrubs overrun the site and only the outline of a platform hints at vanished structures.

dialogue.text: Wood rotted, roofs fell, and time smoothed the earth. Archaeologists now walk Vaishali’s mounds, debating which earthwork hid the old santhagara, while the tank by its side still holds water.

i18n.hi: लकड़ियाँ सड़ गईं, छतें गिरीं, समय ने धरती को समतल कर दिया। आज पुरातत्वविद वैशाली के टीलों पर चलते हैं, बहस करते हैं कि किस मिट्टी के ढेर ने पुराना संथागर छिपा रखा है, जबकि उसके किनारे का पोखर अब भी पानी थामे है।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Saṅghāma’s profile against darkness, half in shadow as if remembered
panels.action: In a half-imagined, half-shadowed scene, Licchavi Saṅghāma’s profile emerges from darkness, his eyes steady, the faint outline of wooden slips and benches behind him like ghosts.

dialogue.text: Today we see only earth and text, yet through them stands a quiet lesson from Vaishali: that even among armed rajas, the unseen power was the rule-bound hall and the small, counted piece of wood.

i18n.hi: आज हमारे सामने सिर्फ ज़मीन और ग्रंथ बचे हैं, पर इन्हीं में से वैशाली की एक चुप सीख उठती है – कि हथियारबंद राजाओं के बीच भी असली ताकत नियम-बँधी सभा और उस छोटी, गिनी हुई लकड़ी की पर्ची में थी।

subtitle_i18n.en: Where Wooden Votes Ruled Warrior Kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ लकड़ी की वोटों से चलते थे योद्धा राजा
